# Dr.-Ing. Maram Abu-Muhfouz

> Process Engineer – Research & Development. PhD in Materials Engineering (Dr.-Ing., RWTH Aachen) based in Düsseldorf, Germany. Research at the Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials (formerly Max Planck Institute for Iron Research, MPIE) on β-FeSi₂ thin films for photovoltaics.

## Key facts
- PhD in Materials Engineering, RWTH Aachen University (2020–2025), research at MPIE Düsseldorf
- Thesis: A Study on the Microstructure Formation Mechanisms and Functional Properties of new β-FeSi₂-based Polycrystalline Thin Films for Photovoltaic Applications Using Correlative Electron Microscopy
- Key PhD results: β-phase fraction 90% ± 10% on 304 stainless steel, grain size 45 ± 25 nm, Ra = 32 nm, first sharp (001)/(010) texture; optimum 1 h, 12.12 nm/min, 500 °C, 1 Pa; 98% ± 2% β on Al₂O₃ (0001)
- Project: up-conversion crystals for perovskite solar cells – best BaF₂:15%Yb³⁺,2%Er³⁺; ~50% Jsc increase at max laser power
- Project: coupled optics–electrical–thermal COMSOL model of a perovskite solar cell
- Dissertation record: https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/1019384
- Expertise: thin-film deposition (DC/RF sputtering, PVD), process-parameter optimisation, microstructure–property correlation
- Characterisation: EBSD, XRD, SEM, ECCI, cathodoluminescence, FIB, STEM, atom probe tomography, AFM, STM/STS, Raman, UV-VIS
- Simulation & programming: COMSOL Multiphysics, MATLAB, Python, C++
- M.Sc. Nanoengineering & Nanoscience with distinction (KIT Karlsruhe & JUST); B.Sc. Electrical Power Engineering
- Awards: CTCN MENA Youth Climate Innovation Award, 1st place (2025, 2022); TUM Open Lab Research Award (2018)
- Languages: German C1, English C1, Arabic native
- Open to: process engineering, R&D engineering and materials science roles (coatings, heat treatment, semiconductors, photovoltaics)
